name: Module 2: encapsulation
source: SPC-NAR (Leonaviciene & Mazutis, NAR 2023) and CapSeq (Baronas et al., Science 2026) via contracts/sources/chip_geometry_requirements.xlsx: 40 um nozzle, 100 / 250 / 700 uL/h, gelation at 4 C for 15-30 min, emulsion breaker + rinse x2, 0.1% LAP, 405 nm for 20 s, 100 um aggregate filter. Wash volumes and flows are placeholders. GENERATED by cad/generators/m2_encapsulation.py.
description: Encapsulate, gel in the cold delay, break the emulsion, rinse, cure, wash, send the capsules on to Module 3.

steps.note: Encapsulate 10,000 capsules: about 541 droplets a second, ~0.08 cells per capsule, so most capsules are empty and almost no occupied capsule holds two cells.
Cold delay: 4 C for 15 min in tubing on a cold block, so the GelMA shells set.
The emulsion (~5.4 uL plus a chase) comes back onto the chip; the capsules settle in one layer on the trap mesh.
Break the emulsion: the oil drains to its own waste, the capsules stay on the mesh.
Rinse twice with buffer, still to the oil waste.
Photoinitiator in (0.1% LAP in the paper).
Cure: 405 nm light for 20 s through the window over the single capsule layer crosslinks the shells.
Wash three times to clear the photoinitiator.
Back-flush from below to lift the capsules off the mesh.
Capsules out through the 100 um aggregate filter to m2_capsule_out_1, on to Module 3.
